text:
The Flames arrived in Edmonton riding a four-game winning streak, and Tristan Jarry ended it by himself. The Oilers goalie stopped all 24 shots for the shutout, and our numbers say he earned more than the zero on the scoreboard. Goals saved above expected, which compares the goals a goalie allowed to the goals the quality of shots against him would normally produce, put Jarry at 2.2 to the good. That is the whole expected-goals total CGY generated, and he turned it away. Jarry was drafted 44th overall by the Penguins in 2013 out of Edmonton, so this one came in his hometown rbuilding.

The game was closer than 4-0 for most of it. Through two periods CGY had the better of the chances in the second, 1.34 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to 0.79, and Martin Pospisil had a 20% look that Jarry stopped. Mattias Ekholm's goal in that period came on a 2% chance, the kind of shot that usually doesn't go in. Mathieu Joseph had opened the scoring in the first on a snap shot, set up by Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard. Then the third period broke it open. EDM out-chanced CGY 1.61 to 0.37, and Kasperi Kapanen scored on the power play at 00:55 before Alex Formenton added another 21 seconds later. McDavid and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins each had two assists, and McDavid's line was on the ice for 1.87 expected goals for against 0.64 against. By deserved-to-win, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, EDM came out at 66%.

For Calgary, the four-game winning streak is over. Dustin Wolf and Devin Cooley shared the net, with Cooley allowing one on nine shots before Wolf took over and gave up three. For Edmonton, it is a clean shutout win at home, built on a goalie who gave the skaters room to wait for their third-period surge.
